name: Metal Backend
description: The Metal RenderBackend: a device and its command queue, capability state behind one lock that no GPU wait holds (fail; recover, which clears a failure only after the health probe passes on a new queue; a health probe that runs one kernel from its own memo; recordCompletion, which marks the backend unhealthy on any command-buffer error; a failed texture allocation also marks it unhealthy), tiled rgba16Float surfaces (one texture per 256 px tile, shared storage on unified memory and managed on a discrete GPU) uploaded from Float32 pixel buffers through HalfFloat with every component clamped to the finite half range and downloaded back, tile eviction under a memory budget (budgetBytes, half the device's recommended working set by default: the least recently used tiles move to a CPU shadow until residentBytes fits, and a read merges resident tiles with shadows), and the pipeline cache: MSL compiled at runtime from string constants, once per PipelineKey (variants from outside go through PipelineKey.validated), memoised in process with Metal's own shader cache across launches; cacheURL is reserved and nothing is read, written or deleted there. Display encode (MB-3, enabled at init) runs the display_encode kernel over resident tiles, reading DisplayTable's thresholds and P3 matrix, and encodes evicted tiles from their shadows on the CPU. Transform (MB-7) runs on the GPU: crop as blit copies and quarter turns as a rotate kernel, piece by piece from TileMap into a new surface (an evicted source tile is copied from its shadow through a temporary texture), with the CPU backend's errors for an invalid crop. Every other op throws unsupported until its slice lands (composite MB-4, blends MB-5 to MB-10, resample MB-8, blur MB-11 and MB-12, adjust MB-13 and MB-14, retouch MB-15).
